mutations.because: The mapping's axes transposed — the one arithmetic error this lane can actually make, and the one that hides best. A hit region is `frame` restated as percentages of the image box; swapping which fraction feeds `left` and which feeds `top` is invisible on any square frame and on any frame whose x happens to equal its y, which is exactly what a hand-written fixture tends to be. Every region still renders, still carries the layer's name, still reports the right layer when clicked, and still costs no fetch — the lane's headline behaviour is completely unharmed. It is wrong only in WHERE the operator has to click, which no assertion about selection can see. So the mapping is pinned axis for axis on a frame whose four fractions are all different, in `hitRegionStyle`'s own suite and again on the rendered buttons.

The hit region outliving the thing it is a region for. `enabled: false` is not a style: X9's rule is that a disabled layer renders exactly what the same template WITHOUT that layer renders, so the compositor draws nothing in that box at all. Dropping the term reads like tidying a redundant condition — the layer is still in the template, its elements still declare frames, and the editor still lists it — and it produces an invisible button over bare canvas that selects a layer nothing on screen shows. The gesture even 'works': the row lights up. It is caught only by asking what a DISABLED layer declares, which is why the exclusion has a test of its own rather than being described in a comment. (Re-anchored by CE2: the `enabled !== false` term was hoisted out of the html-only filter so it governs the ground kinds' whole-canvas regions too. Same claim, same test, one term instead of two — dropping it now makes EVERY disabled layer clickable, so the mutation is strictly stronger than the one CE1 ran.) (Re-anchored by AR2: html layers no longer declare hit regions, so the disabled-layer proof is the ground's own test. Same filter, same claim.)
command: a disabled ground layer is not clickable

mutations.because: The second selection concept, in the shape someone would actually introduce it: an element is a finer thing than a layer, so reporting the element rather than its layer looks like more precision, not less. Under it the canvas keeps its own selection perfectly — the clicked region goes pressed, a second click moves it, nothing throws — and the list below simply never lights up, because no row is named `html-0`. That is precisely the divergence the lane exists to prevent: one selection reached two ways, or two selections that agree until they do not. The component suite does catch it too (`onSelectLayer.mock.calls` is compared exactly, and `html-0` is not `html`) — but only because that assertion is exact; relax it to `toHaveBeenCalled` and the defect walks through, because the callback IS called, with a plausible id. The command below is the editor's, deliberately: it is the one that asserts the CLASS rather than the argument — that whatever the canvas reports, the row lights up.
command: clicking the creative lights the row
